## Resolved

### F-415 — A released db adapter imported nothing, so no schema existed

> _2026-10-07 · core/blong-server · resolved_

The release block of the db adapter escaped its import patterns one level too deep (a literal
backslash before every dot), so /\\.db$/ matched no group name and a deployed process attached no
schema contributor, no model and no fixture: the adapter connected, synced nothing, and the first
seed insert died on a missing core_type. Every table list in the cluster was empty and login
answered Knex Error, which is what sent the tenant hunt through resolvers and volumes. The
microservice and dev blocks beside it hold the same patterns spelled correctly, so the two differ by
one backslash and nothing verified the released spelling.

The release imports now read exactly like microservice and dev; the migration step of a release-only
deployment created the schema (24 tables) that login then used.

### F-435 — A handler call made while the process is loading goes over the socket

> _2026-10-08 · core/blong-server · resolved_

core/blong-server/orchestrator/subject/validation.ts called `handler['subjectModelList']({}, {})`
inside the validation factory, and the module is not attached to the `srv.subject` port: the port's
`createHandlers` is called with `kind=handler` and `kind=model`, never `kind=validation`, and the
map a sibling handler of the same folder could see through the config was not visible to it (F-437).
So the proxy the module holds is not the port's, `handles` answers false for its own namespace, and
the call is dispatched over the socket — while the process is still loading. In the dev cluster it
appeared as `method: subject.model.list` with `connect ECONNREFUSED 10.43.178.61:8091` (the stale
`subject` Service), and after that Service was deleted, as
`getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND subject.blong-suite.svc.cluster.local`: the error text followed the cluster,
the defect did not. Pods of the same artifact that log `srv.subject dispatch event adapter.ready`
before the validation never make the call at all, which is why most of them served while a few
crash-looped. Lesson: a call through the handler proxy from a module that no port owns is a network
call, and its failure arrives as a connection error rather than as a name that is simply not there.

orchestrator/subject/validation.ts now reads the collected models from subjectModels.ts
(subjectModelFind) instead of calling the sibling through the proxy, which is the route this entry
named. Verified on the dev cluster: the four tenant deployments reached Available, the migration Job
completed, and the whole k3d cycle ran green — the boot no longer dials a namespace no process
answers.

### F-437 — The local read that looks equivalent to the call publishes no validations

> _2026-10-08 · core/blong-server · resolved_

The tempting fix for F-435 is to read the collected models instead of calling `subjectModelList`.
The first attempt read `config.context.subjectModels`, which is the port's own slot, and saw zero
models while the port had already collected thirteen. The order was never in question: measured on
`realm/blong-gateway` with a temporary log on both sides, the port collected models 1 to 13 at lines
48 to 73 of the run and the validation factory read the map at line 110. The view was the problem —
the validation module is not attached to the `srv.subject` port, so the `config` it is handed is a
slice of its own module and never carries what the port wrote. Lesson: the config a definition reads
is owned by the module that carries it, and two files in one folder can be owned by different
things; a shared module is what makes a writer and a reader agree, which is what `subjectModels.ts`
now is.

Resolved by D-459: the collected models live in core/blong-server/subjectModels.ts, a module at the
package root rather than a slot on the port's config, so the port's writes are what the validation
reads. The lesson stands and is what the friction was kept for; the 13-against-zero disagreement it
describes is gone.
